messages:
Priya: Heads-up - running int8 bring-up for reranker-v4. Initial offline bench shows per-lang NDCG@5 drop in JP and DE but EN stable. Anyone seen language-specific quant sensitivity before?
Tom: Not usually that split. Can you paste the slice numbers?
Priya: Sure: baseline fp16 NDCG@5 -> EN=0.523, JP=0.491, DE=0.477. int8 candidate: EN=0.521, JP=0.462, DE=0.449. MRR@10 similar pattern.
Riley: That's a >0.02 drop in JP/DE NDCG, sizeable. Are we using the same dataset tokenization + unicode normalization across langs? Locale differences can change token counts a lot.
Priya: We used the new unified normalizer from ingest v3 which applies NFKC and lowercasing for latin scripts, but for CJK we only apply NFKC. Maybe that change affects short JP queries where punctuation was informative.
Jules: Also check if we accidentally used different candidate pools for those slices. The offline harness has a fallback that fetches "expanded" candidates for non-EN locales unless flagged.
Priya: Good catch. Eval command I ran: 
```
ci-run-eval --model reranker_v4_int8 --baseline reranker_v4_fp16 --cohorts en,jp,de --metrics ndcg@5,mrr@10 --samples 8k --seed 42
```
Tom: Can you re-run with `--preserve-candidate-pool true --token-normalizer legacy` to match baseline? Also try `--quant-decode-mode deterministic` in case stochastic fast paths differ.
Riley: We should also compare token lengths distribution between baseline and int8 runs. Quant kernels sometimes truncate or pad differently if sequence length bucketing changed.
Priya: Re-run queued with those flags. Also toggling `kvpack=false` per Lee's earlier suggestion - want to rule out pack-time packing changes.
ci-bot: ci-bot: Eval job 96211 queued by Priya.
Tom: If the re-run still shows language gaps, propose we run a small online A/B (5% traffic) for EN vs JP vs DE partitioned by locale and enable fp16 fallback for locales with >0.015 NDCG regression.
Jules: Agree but let's avoid online until we confirm candidate/tok parity - we had one misrouted canary last quarter. Add a golden set per-language (1k queries each) capturing short/long and punctuation-heavy queries.
Priya: Re-run results: with preserve-candidate-pool + legacy normalizer + kvpack=false -> EN=0.522, JP=0.489, DE=0.473. JP/DE improved but still ~0.002-0.004 delta vs baseline.
Riley: That's much better. Looks like the normalizer and candidate selection were the dominant factors. Remaining tiny gap could be quant noise; add confidence intervals with bootstrapping.
Tom: Agree on CI. Also open PR to pin normalizer in the deployment manifest for int8 bringup until we validate. Add a unit test to eval harness to assert candidate pool parity by locale.
Jules: I'll add the golden sets to the quality monitor and configure alert for per-locale NDCG@5 drop > 0.01. Also tracking MRR@10 threshold > 0.012.
Priya: Action list: (1) Tom pins normalizer in manifest, (2) Riley will add token-length hist check to eval summary, (3) Jules uploads golden locales & alert rules, (4) I'll run CI bootstrapped CIs and then we decide on a small A/B if still necessary.
ci-bot: ci-bot: Eval job 96211 completed (status: success). Artifacts: /artifacts/96211/summary.html
Tom: Nice triage. Also leave a short note in ops with the exact manifest diff so ops can rollback quickly if later we see online drift.
Priya: Will do. Thanks all :thumbsup:
